## The runtime registry

A runtime is one backend. It is an engine such as llama.cpp, or a hosted
API, together with the
[`Chat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat) subclass
that talks to it. urai contains no runtimes. A backend package such as
rishi calls
[`register_runtime`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#register_runtime)
with a [`Runtime`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#runtime)
for each one. The `cls` field is a dotted path string, or the class
itself for a backend that you define in your own code. A dotted path is
not imported until a chat for that runtime is built.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th><a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#runtime"><code>Runtime</code></a>
field</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>name</code></td>
<td>The name of the runtime</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>cls</code></td>
<td>The <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat"><code>Chat</code></a>
subclass that implements the runtime</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>pats</code></td>
<td>Substrings that mark a model name as belonging to the runtime, such
as <code>.gguf</code> for llama.cpp</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>optional</code></td>
<td><code>True</code> for a backend that needs a pip extra</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>extra</code></td>
<td>The pip extra that installs the backend. The default is
<code>name</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>local</code></td>
<td><code>True</code> when the runtime runs on this machine</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>caps</code></td>
<td>A function <code>caps(model, model_path)</code> that returns the <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#caps"><code>Caps</code></a>
of a model, or its dotted path</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ctx</code></td>
<td>A fixed context window, for a runtime whose models all have the same
window</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The `install` property of a
[`Runtime`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#runtime) is the
pip command that installs the backend. A caller can show it when the
backend is missing. `register_runtime(rt, dflt=True)` also makes `rt`
the runtime that a bare
[`Chat()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat) uses.

Runtimes are tried in the order of registration. Ollama names a Hugging
Face GGUF repository as `hf.co/...-GGUF`. This name also contains
`gguf`. Register Ollama before llama.cpp. Otherwise llama.cpp takes
every such name for a local file. The example registers three
placeholder runtimes, so the rest of this page runs without a real
backend.

### Runtime

``` python
def Runtime(
    name:str, cls:object, pats:tuple=(), optional:bool=False, extra:str='', local:bool=True, caps:object=None,
    ctx:int=0
)->None:
```

*One registered backend: the
[`Chat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat) class that

## Naming a model

Three rules say which runtime a model needs. They apply in this order.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Rule</th>
<th>Example</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>An explicit <code>runtime=</code> argument</td>
<td><code>runtime='llama'</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>A runtime name as a prefix of the model name</td>
<td><code>llama/qwen3-4b</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>A match between the model name and the <code>pats</code> of a
runtime</td>
<td><code>qwen3-4b.gguf</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

[`split_runtime`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#split_runtime)
removes a prefix only when the prefix names a registered runtime. The
name `openai/gpt-5.1` keeps its vendor prefix.
[`infer_runtime`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#infer_runtime)
returns the first registered runtime whose `pats` match the name. It
returns `None` when none match.

`resolve_runtime(model, runtime, model_path)` applies the three rules
and returns `(runtime, model)`. When the model name gives no match, it
tries `model_path` against the `pats`. When neither `model` nor
`model_path` is given, it returns the default runtime. When it cannot
decide, it raises `ValueError`. The message lists all three ways to name
the runtime.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/opts.py#L63"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
):
```

*Work out `(runtime, model)` from an explicit `runtime`, a `runtime/`

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/opts.py#L50"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### split_runtime

``` python
def split_runtime(
    model
):
```

*Split `'runtime/model'` into `(runtime, model)` when the prefix names a
registered runtime.*

``` python
test_eq(split_runtime('llama/qwen3-4b'), ('llama', 'qwen3-4b'))
test_eq(split_runtime('openai/gpt-5.1'), (None, 'openai/gpt-5.1'))   # 'openai' is not a runtime
test_eq(split_runtime('plain'), (None, 'plain'))
```

``` python
test_eq(infer_runtime('qwen3-4b.gguf'), 'llama')
test_eq(infer_runtime('hf.co/unsloth/qwen3-GGUF'), 'ollama')  # registered first, so it wins
test_eq(infer_runtime('gpt-5.1'), 'remote')
test_eq(infer_runtime('mystery-model'), None)
```

``` python
test_eq(resolve_runtime('gpt-5.1'), ('remote', 'gpt-5.1'))
test_eq(resolve_runtime('llama/anything'), ('llama', 'anything'))
test_eq(resolve_runtime('anything', runtime='llama'), ('llama', 'anything'))
test_eq(resolve_runtime(), ('remote', None))                   # nothing named: the default
test_eq(resolve_runtime(None, model_path='/m/x.gguf'), ('llama', None))
```

``` python
test_fail(lambda: resolve_runtime('mystery'), contains="Can't tell which backend")
test_fail(lambda: resolve_runtime('x', runtime='nope'), contains='Unknown runtime')
```

## A resolved model

`resolve(name, runtime, model_path, ctx, **opts)` works out what is
known about a model without loading it. It returns a
[`ModelSpec`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#modelspec).

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th><a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#modelspec"><code>ModelSpec</code></a>
field</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>name</code></td>
<td>The name that the caller typed. It falls back to the model id, then
the runtime name</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>runtime</code></td>
<td>The name of the runtime</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>model_id</code></td>
<td>The id that the backend receives</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ctx</code></td>
<td>The context window in tokens</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>note</code></td>
<td>Text about how the model was resolved. It is empty when the window
is known</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>opts</code></td>
<td>The keyword options that were passed to <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#resolve"><code>resolve</code></a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The `local` property of a
[`ModelSpec`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#modelspec) is
`True` when the runtime runs on this machine.

The `ctx` argument decides the window first. When you do not pass it,
[`resolve`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#resolve) takes
the window from the first rule in this table that applies.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Rule</th>
<th><code>ctx</code></th>
<th><code>note</code></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>The runtime sets <code>ctx</code></td>
<td>The <code>ctx</code> of the runtime</td>
<td><code>''</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The runtime is local</td>
<td><code>DFLT_CTX</code> (128,000)</td>
<td><code>''</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The runtime is hosted</td>
<td>The first value of the pair that <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#hosted_ctx"><code>hosted_ctx</code></a>
returns</td>
<td>The second value of that pair. It says when the window is
assumed</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

A [`ModelSpec`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#modelspec)
is frozen. You can cache it, compare it and pass it between parts of a
program. Pass it to
[`mk_chat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#mk_chat) or
[`Chat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat). The `opts`
field does not take part in comparisons. Two specs for the same model
compare equal when only their `opts` differ.

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

*Resolve `name` to a

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/opts.py#L76"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### ModelSpec

``` python
def ModelSpec(
    name:str, runtime:str, model_id:str, ctx:int=128000, note:str='', opts:dict=<factory>
)->None:
```

*A resolved model: its runtime, the id the backend is given, and its
context window.*

``` python
s = resolve('gpt-5.1')
test_eq((s.name, s.runtime, s.model_id, s.local), ('gpt-5.1', 'remote', 'gpt-5.1', False))
assert s.ctx > 100_000 and s.note == ''
test_eq(str(s), 'gpt-5.1 (gpt-5.1)')
```

``` python
s = resolve('llama/qwen3-4b', ctx=8192, n_gpu_layers=99)
test_eq((s.runtime, s.model_id, s.ctx, s.opts), ('llama', 'qwen3-4b', 8192, {'n_gpu_layers': 99}))
test_eq(s.local, True)
test_eq(resolve('unknown-hosted', runtime='remote').note,
        'context window unknown, assuming 128k')
```

``` python
# `opts` is out of the comparison: the same model twice is the same model
test_eq(resolve('gpt-5.1', temp=0.1), resolve('gpt-5.1', temp=0.9))
test_eq(resolve('gpt-5.1') == resolve('gpt-4o'), False)
```

## Capabilities

`model_caps(model, runtime, model_path)` returns the
[`Caps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#caps) of a model
without loading the model. It resolves the runtime and calls the `caps`
function of that runtime when one is registered. The table shows the
other cases.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Case</th>
<th>Result</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>The runtime cannot be resolved, or is not registered</td>
<td><code>hosted_caps(model)</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>A hosted runtime with no <code>caps</code> function</td>
<td><code>hosted_caps(model)</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>A local runtime with no <code>caps</code> function</td>
<td>An unknown <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#caps"><code>Caps()</code></a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The <code>caps</code> function raises an error or returns
nothing</td>
<td>An unknown <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#caps"><code>Caps()</code></a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

[`model_caps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#model_caps)
never raises, so a failed check does not stop a chat from starting.
[`load_ref`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#load_ref)
imports an object from a dotted path such as `'pkg.mod.name'`. It
returns a value that is not a string unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/opts.py#L108"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
    model:NoneType=None, runtime:NoneType=None, model_path:NoneType=None

```

*The [`Caps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/caps.html#caps) of

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/opts.py#L102"

### load_ref

``` python
def load_ref(
    o
):
```

*Import and return the object at dotted path `o`, or return `o` if it is
not a string.*

``` python
test_eq(model_caps('gpt-5.1').source, 'fastllm')
test_eq(model_caps('qwen3-4b.gguf').source, 'default')     # local, no prober registered
test_eq(model_caps('gpt-5.1', runtime='nope').source, 'fastllm')  # unknown runtime, still asked
```

## Options

[`ChatOpts`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#chatopts)
holds every setting that a chat can take. Each setting has one portable
name that all runtimes share. The fields fall into four groups.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Group</th>
<th>Fields</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Conversation</td>
<td><code>sp</code> (system prompt), <code>tools</code>,
<code>messages</code> (history to start from)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Tool loop</td>
<td><code>approve</code>, <code>max_steps</code>,
<code>tool_max_len</code>, <code>parallel_tools</code>,
<code>max_parallel_tools</code>, <code>final_prompt</code>,
<code>cbs</code>, <code>default_cbs</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Generation</td>
<td><code>ctx</code>, <code>max_output_tokens</code>, <code>temp</code>,
<code>top_k</code>, <code>top_p</code>, <code>seed</code>,
<code>think</code>, <code>effort</code>, <code>tool_mode</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Credentials</td>
<td><code>api_key</code>, <code>api_key_env</code>,
<code>base_url</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`approve` is a function that takes a tool call and returns `True` when
the call may run. The default `None` runs every call. `max_steps` is the
number of tool calls that one turn can use. `final_prompt` is sent to
the model when that budget runs out. `api_key_env` names an environment
variable that holds the key. A saved configuration can then omit the
key. The `extra` field holds options that no portable field covers.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Field</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>think</code></td>
<td><code>False</code> asks a reasoning model not to deliberate. The
default <code>None</code> leaves the option unset.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>effort</code></td>
<td>How much a reasoning model deliberates, such as <code>'low'</code>,
<code>'medium'</code> or <code>'high'</code>, for models that grade it.
The default <code>''</code> leaves the option unset.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>tool_mode</code></td>
<td>How tool schemas reach the model. <code>'native'</code> sends them
as part of the request. <code>'tags'</code> writes them into the
prompt.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>cbs</code></td>
<td>Callbacks that the chat attaches, after the default callbacks.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>default_cbs</code></td>
<td>When <code>True</code>, the chat first attaches the callbacks that
its backend lists in <code>_dflt_cbs</code>. The default is
<code>True</code>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`ChatOpts.create(opts, **kw)` builds a
[`ChatOpts`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#chatopts) from
an existing
[`ChatOpts`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#chatopts) or a
dict, plus keyword overrides. `ALIASES` translates the older names that
backends used.

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Older name</th>
<th>Portable name</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>reasoning_effort</code></td>
<td><code>effort</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>temperature</code></td>
<td><code>temp</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>max_tokens</code></td>
<td><code>max_output_tokens</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ctx_limit</code>, <code>n_ctx</code></td>
<td><code>ctx</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>system</code></td>
<td><code>sp</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

A keyword with no field of its own goes into `extra`. A backend receives
`extra` unchanged. Backend-only settings such as `n_gpu_layers` are
passed through `extra`.

`set()` returns a dict of the fields whose value differs from the
default, without `extra`. A field that you set to its default value does
not appear. `set()` cannot tell it from a field that you did not set.
The `key` property returns `api_key`, or the value of the environment
variable that `api_key_env` names. It stores nothing on the object.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/opts.py#L132"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### ChatOpts

``` python
def ChatOpts(
    sp:str='', tools:tuple=(), messages:tuple=(), approve:object=None, max_steps:int=10, tool_max_len:int=0,
    parallel_tools:bool=False, max_parallel_tools:int=0,
    final_prompt:str="You've reached the tool-call budget for this turn. Stop calling tools and answer with what you already have.",
    cbs:tuple=(), default_cbs:bool=True, ctx:int=0, max_output_tokens:int=0, temp:float=None, top_k:int=None,
    top_p:float=None, seed:int=None, think:bool=None, effort:str='', tool_mode:str='', api_key:str='',
    api_key_env:str='', base_url:str='', extra:dict=<factory>
)->None:
```

*Every chat setting under the portable name all runtimes share.*

``` python
o = ChatOpts.create(sp='Be brief.', temp=0.2)
test_eq((o.sp, o.temp, o.max_steps), ('Be brief.', 0.2, 10))
test_eq(o.set(), {'sp': 'Be brief.', 'temp': 0.2})
```

``` python
o = ChatOpts.create(temp=0.2, n_gpu_layers=99)
test_eq(o.extra, {'n_gpu_layers': 99})
test_eq(ChatOpts.create(o, temp=0.9).temp, 0.9)
test_eq(ChatOpts.create(o, seed=1).extra, {'n_gpu_layers': 99})
```

``` python
import os
os.environ['DEMO_KEY'] = 'sk-secret'
test_eq(ChatOpts.create(api_key_env='DEMO_KEY').key, 'sk-secret')
test_eq(ChatOpts.create(api_key='explicit', api_key_env='DEMO_KEY').key, 'explicit')
test_eq(ChatOpts.create(api_key_env='NOT_SET_ANYWHERE').key, None)
test_eq(ChatOpts().key, None)
del os.environ['DEMO_KEY']
```

``` python
test_eq(ChatOpts.create(reasoning_effort='high').effort, 'high')
test_eq(ChatOpts.create(temperature=0.2).temp, 0.2)
test_eq(ChatOpts.create(max_tokens=512).max_output_tokens, 512)
test_eq(ChatOpts.create(ctx_limit=8192).ctx, 8192)
test_eq(ChatOpts.create(n_ctx=8192).ctx, 8192)
test_eq(ChatOpts.create(system='Be brief.').sp, 'Be brief.')
test_eq(ChatOpts.create(reasoning_effort='high').extra, {})   # aliased, not shunted into extra
```

``` python
test_eq(ChatOpts.create({'sp': 'from a dict'}).sp, 'from a dict')
o = ChatOpts.create({'temperature': 0.5, 'custom': 1, 'extra': {'a': 2}}, extra={'b': 3}, temp=0.7)
test_eq((o.temp, o.extra), (0.7, {'a': 2, 'b': 3, 'custom': 1}))   # dicts take aliases and extras like keywords
test_eq(ChatOpts.create({'temp': .2, 'temperature': .3}, temp=.9).temp, .9)   # keywords win even through an alias
test_eq(ChatOpts.create(), ChatOpts())
test_eq(ChatOpts().set(), {})
```

## Translating for a backend

A backend translates the portable names with two class attributes on its
[`Chat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat) subclass.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Attribute</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>_opt_map</code></td>
<td>A dict from a portable name to the name that the backend uses</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>_opt_skip</code></td>
<td>The options that the backend cannot use</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

[`Chat.map_opts`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat.map_opts),
on the [chat](chat.html) page, applies both. It drops a skipped option
without a warning. It renames every other option and passes it on. A
target name with a dot in it is nested. The entry
`{'ctx': 'eng_kw.max_num_tokens'}` sends the window as
`eng_kw={'max_num_tokens': ...}`.
[`set_dotted`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#set_dotted)
builds the nested dict.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### set_dotted

``` python
def set_dotted(
    d, path, v
):
```

*Set `d['a']['b'] = v` for `path='a.b'`, creating the dicts in between.*

``` python
test_eq(set_dotted({}, 'eng_kw.max_num_tokens', 8192), {'eng_kw': {'max_num_tokens': 8192}})
test_eq(set_dotted({'eng_kw': {'a': 1}}, 'eng_kw.b', 2), {'eng_kw': {'a': 1, 'b': 2}})
test_eq(set_dotted({}, 'plain', 1), {'plain': 1})
```

## One turn at a time

Some settings can change between two calls without a new chat. Examples
are a higher `effort` for a hard question and `temp=0` for an
extraction. `GEN_OPTS` lists these settings: `max_output_tokens`,
`temp`, `top_k`, `top_p`, `seed`, `think`, `effort` and `tool_mode`.

`turn_kw(opts, **kw)` builds a
[`ChatOpts`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#chatopts) from
`opts` and `kw`. It returns the fields of `GEN_OPTS` that differ from
their defaults, and all `extra` options. It leaves out the other fields,
such as the system prompt `sp`, which apply to the whole chat.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/opts.py#L201"

### turn_kw

``` python
def turn_kw(
    opts:NoneType=None, **kw
):
```

*The settings in `opts` and `kw` that can apply to a single turn, plus
any `extra` options.*

``` python
test_eq(turn_kw(temp=0.9, effort='high'), {'temp': 0.9, 'effort': 'high'})
test_eq(turn_kw(temp=0.9, sp='ignored here'), {'temp': 0.9})
test_eq(turn_kw(), {})
test_eq(turn_kw(ChatOpts(temp=0.1), temp=0.9), {'temp': 0.9})
```
